prose.heading: Audit logs and the Score Change Log

prose.text: {{score-change-log}} {{score-change-fields}} {{csv-times-pdt}} Retention and the console time zone are not stated on these pages {{gap:log-retention-timezone}}. The factor and entity overrides that the audit logs capture are in [[risk360.scoring]].

checks.do: Whether the domains were added to Seeds Management and 24–48 hours have passed since they were added, when asking about scan results for those domains.
Whether the admin's role has Administrator Management or Remote Assistance Management access at the level the task needs.
That times in the CSV downloaded from the audit logs or the Score Change Log are in PDT.

setup-steps.statement: The configuration guide for Risk360 has four steps: role-based administration, domains for external attack surface analysis, peer score and financial risk settings, and alerting rules that trigger when a preset threshold is reached.

quotes: Step 1: Configure Role-Based Administration
Step 2: Configure Domains for External Attack Surface Analysis
Step 3: Manage Peer Score and Financial Risk Settings
Step 4: Configure Alerting
Configure rules to trigger alerts when a preset threshold is reached.
You can customize the parameters used to calculate your industry's peer risk score and your organization's financial exposure.

admin-role-flow.statement: For an organization enabled with Authentication Service, Authentication Service users are assigned as Risk360 service admins: add the Risk360 admin role in Experience Center, add the users in the Authentication Service Admin Portal, then assign them a Risk360 admin role.

quotes: Your organization is enabled with Authentication Service and you must assign Authentication Service users as Risk360 service admins:
Add Risk360 admin role in Experience Center.
Add users in the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
Assign users a Risk360 admin role.

seed-weekly-scan.statement: Seeds Management scans the added domains weekly to identify publicly exposed assets, and shows the risk quantified for them as factors on the Factors page.

quotes: the Risk360 service performs weekly scans to identify publicly exposed assets within the domains for potential cyberattacks
The Risk360 service also quantifies the risk determined on various parameters for the exposed assets and visualizes them as factors on the Factors page.

seed-domain-limit.statement: Up to 10 domains can be added for scanning, whether one at a time or from a CSV file.

quotes: You can add up to 10 domains for scanning.
You can add up to 10 domains.
You can add up to 10 domains.

seed-scan-latency.statement: After domains are added (singly or from a CSV file), the Risk360 service takes up to 24–48 hours to scan and analyze them.

quotes: the Risk360 service takes up to 24–48 hours to scan and analyze the domains.
The Risk360 service takes up to 24–48 hours to scan and analyze the domains.
The Risk360 service takes up to 24–48 hours to scan and analyze the domains.

seed-location.statement: The Seeds Management page is under Administration > Legacy Admin Management > Risk360.

quotes: On the Seeds Management page (Administration > Legacy Admin Management > Risk360)

seed-csv.statement: Domains are bulk-added by downloading a CSV template, listing the domains, uploading the file and clicking Save after a successful-upload message; on an error, the domains must be in the correct format in the CSV file before reuploading.

quotes: Click Download CSV Template. A CSV template for uploading the domains is downloaded to your device.
After a successful upload message is displayed, click Save.
If an error message is displayed, ensure that the domains are added in the correct format in the CSV file and reupload the file.

role-default-super-admin.statement: Zscaler provides a default super admin role with full access to Risk360, assigned to the default admin and assignable to other admins.

quotes: Zscaler provides a default super admin role that has full access to the Risk360. This role is assigned to the default admin, but you can assign this role to other admins as necessary.

role-hierarchy.statement: The About Role Management page says role assignment maintains hierarchy so an admin can't modify the settings of an admin with a broader scope, and that the Role Management page lets an admin edit a configured admin role with lesser scope.

quotes: Assign roles to admins to maintain hierarchy among the admins so that the admin can't modify the settings of an admin with a broader scope.
Edit a configured admin role with lesser scope.

role-prerequisites.statement: Configuring a Risk360 admin role requires the proper permissions to configure a role and organizational scope.

quotes: You must have the proper permissions to configure a role.
You must have organizational scope.

role-permission-dashboard-users.statement: In a Risk360 admin role, Dashboard and User Management permissions are each View Only or None; View Only allows viewing the dashboard or the User Management page respectively.

quotes: View Only: Allows admins to view the dashboard.
None: Doesn’t allow access to the dashboard.
View Only: Allows admins to view the User Management page.
None: Doesn’t allow access to the User Management page.

role-permission-admin-mgmt.statement: In a Risk360 admin role, Administrator Management is Full, View Only or None; Full covers adding, editing and deleting admin accounts, viewing auditors, configuring password expiration and SAML single sign-on for admins, and, under Role Management, adding, editing and deleting only roles that have equal or lesser scope.

quotes: Administrators: Admins can add, edit, and delete admin accounts.
Auditors: Admins can view the auditors.
Administrator Management: Admins can configure password expiration and SAML single sign-on for admins.
Role Management: Admins can only add, edit, and delete roles that have equal or lesser scope.
View Only: Allows admins to view, but not edit, the following pages.
None: Doesn’t allow admins access to Administration Management.

role-permission-remote-assistance.statement: Remote Assistance Management lets admins allow Zscaler Support to log in remotely to the Zscaler Admin Console; its permission in a Risk360 role is Full, View Only or None.

quotes: In Remote Assistance Management, admins can allow Zscaler Support to securely and remotely log in to your Zscaler Admin Console.
Full: Allows admins to access the Remote Assistance.
View Only: Allows admins to view the Remote Assistance.
None: Doesn’t allow access to the Remote Assistance.

role-page-columns.statement: The Role Management page (Administration > Role Management > Risk360) lists each role's Full Access areas, View-Only Access areas and Name.

quotes: On the Role Management page (Administration > Role Management > Risk360)
Full Access: The areas of Risk360 where admins with this role have full access.
View-Only Access: The areas of Risk360 where admins with this role have view-only access.
Name: The name of the role.

audit-records.statement: Zscaler records the login name and IP address of every user who changes configuration settings; the Risk360 Audit Logs page is under Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Risk360.

quotes: Zscaler records the login name and IP address of every user who changes configuration settings.
On the Audit Logs page (Data Explorer > Audit Logs > Risk360)

audit-filters.statement: Risk360 audit logs can be searched by Resource, Admin ID or Client IP and filtered by Time Range, Action, Category, Sub-Category, Interface or Result.

quotes: Search for the logs by Resource, Admin ID, or Client IP.
Filter logs by Time Range, Action, Category, Sub-Category, Interface, or Result.

audit-fields.statement: Audit log entries carry Interface (UI or API based) and Result (Success, Failure or Partially Failed).

quotes: Interface: How the user performed their actions. The interface is either UI or API based.
Result: The outcome of an action (Success, Failure, or Partially Failed).

csv-times-pdt.statement: Times in the CSV downloaded from the Risk360 Audit Logs page and from the Score Change Log page are in PDT.

quotes: The times mentioned in the CSV file are in PDT.
The times mentioned in the CSV file are in PDT.

score-change-log.statement: The Score Change Log page (Data Explorer > Risk360 > Score Change Log) records risk score changes across categories and factors and can be filtered by Change Event, Category, Factor Group or Factor.

quotes: The Score Change Log page (Data Explorer > Risk360 > Score Change Log) records the risk score change logs across categories and factors.
Filter Data: Filter logs by Change Event, Category, Factor Group, or Factor.

score-change-fields.statement: Each score change log row has a Change Event (override, weight or score), Risk Category (External Attack Surface, Compromise, Lateral Propagation or Data Loss), Factor Group, Factor, Notes, Previous Value and Current Value.

quotes: Change Event: The event that affected the risk score (override, weight, or score).
Risk Category: The Risk360 category where the change occurred (External Attack Surface, Compromise, Lateral Propagation, or Data Loss).
Previous Value: The score before the event.
Current Value: The current score after the event.
Factor Group: The factor group that is affected.
Factor: The factor that is affected.
Notes: Any additional information about the event.

role-edit-scope.summary: The About Role Management page and the Add Role page state the scope of roles an admin can edit differently.

positions.says: An admin can edit a configured admin role with lesser scope.

quotes: Edit a configured admin role with lesser scope.

positions.says: With Role Management access, an admin can add, edit and delete roles that have equal or lesser scope.

quotes: Role Management: Admins can only add, edit, and delete roles that have equal or lesser scope.

role-edit-scope.impact: Whether an admin can edit a role of equal scope is not settled; do not state it either way.

seed-scope.title: Whether Seeds Management enumerates subdomains and what happens past 10 domains
seed-scope.detail: The captured pages give the weekly scan and the 10-domain limit but do not state a value for the page's View scan frequency, whether subdomains are enumerated, or what happens when more than 10 domains are added.

role-access-areas.title: Which Risk360 areas the Full Access and View-Only Access columns cover
role-access-areas.detail: The role pages list Dashboard, Administrator Management, User Management and Remote Assistance Management permissions; they do not say whether alerts, financial risk or reports fall under any of them, or what the Full Access and View-Only Access columns cover beyond those.

log-retention-timezone.title: Audit log and Score Change Log retention and console time zone
log-retention-timezone.detail: The captured pages state that CSV times are in PDT but not how long these logs are kept or which time zone the console shows; they do not define each Change Event value (override, weight, score) individually. The overview's logs-retention claim (risk360.overview:logs-retention) gives a rolling retention of up to a year for Risk360 logs generally, without saying whether it covers these two logs.
